title: Apple HomeView Puts Siri AI on a Shared Screen in the Home
excerpt: Apple's $299 HomeView display recognises six household members by face and gives each a personal screen, with Siri AI handling requests — as long as a paired iPhone is nearby.
body:
• Apple HomeView is a $299 seven-inch smart display in tabletop and wall-mounted versions, on sale November 13 in eight markets including India and the US.
  • The screen recognises up to six household members by face and shows each person their own Home Screen, apps and widgets.
  • Siri AI handles general requests on the device, but questions drawing on your messages or calendar need a paired Apple Intelligence iPhone or iPad nearby.
  • HomeView is not sold in the European Union, where Apple says Siri AI is currently unavailable on iOS.

Apple has moved its AI assistant off the phone and onto a screen that stays in the room. HomeView, announced on October 13 and flagged in UC Today's weekly coverage of the sector, is a seven-inch touchscreen for music, video calls and controlling connected home accessories. It comes in two forms at the same $299 price: a tabletop model on an aluminium speaker base, and a wall-mounted version. Pre-orders are open in Australia, Canada, India, New Zealand, the UK and the US, with availability from November 13, according to Tech-ish's launch report.

A shared screen that knows who is standing in front of it

The problem HomeView is built to solve is that household screens serve everyone, while phones serve one person. HomeView recognises up to six enrolled people as they approach and loads a personal Home Screen for each, with their own apps and widgets. Guests are not locked out: they can control accessories, check the weather, set timers and play music without an Apple Account and without seeing anyone else's information. A personalised experience requires an Apple Account, a compatible iPhone or iPad, and membership of the shared home in Apple's Home app.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=PvQ1jXgDsFM

"Apple HomeView is designed to be shared by everyone in the home yet feel completely personal to each user."

— Greg Joswiak, Apple's senior vice president of Worldwide Marketing

Both models run on Apple's A18 chip with a square 1088-by-1088 display, True Tone and brightness that drops to 0.3 nits for a dark bedroom. A 12MP Center Stage camera keeps participants framed on FaceTime calls. The Home Camera view can stream up to nine camera feeds at once, and the device controls lights, locks, blinds and thermostats through HomeKit and Matter, with Thread networking for supported accessories.

Siri AI, with the phone still doing the personal work

Siri AI, Apple's rebuilt conversational assistant powered by Apple Intelligence, is the centre of the pitch. General knowledge and music requests work on the device itself. Anything that draws on your own messages, calendar or reminders needs a paired Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad, recently unlocked and present, with setup requiring iOS 27.2 or iPadOS 27.2 or later. Apple says Secure Exclaves in the A18 chip process camera and microphone data for recognition separately from the operating system, and that Private Cloud Compute handles some remote requests without storing data.

The limits matter as much as the features. Some server-based Apple Intelligence functions carry daily usage limits, and Apple says expanded access will cost extra in future, without yet giving a price or start date. Camera features such as encrypted recording and natural-language video search need compatible cameras and an iCloud+ subscription. The wall model also needs a mount and power accessories sold separately; Schneider Home mounts start at $59.95.

Part of a wider home push

HomeView did not arrive alone. Apple's October home lineup includes HomePod mini 2 at $149 from October 30 and a fourth-generation Apple TV 4K at $299, also on November 13, plus an Apple Home Collection of LG and Schneider Electric accessories — cameras, thermostats, a doorbell and a lock — starting in December, MacObserver's announcement coverage reports. Siri AI also reaches older Apple TV 4K models as a beta in tvOS 27.2. Together the launches put Apple into direct competition with Amazon's Alexa and Ring products and Google's Nest ecosystem, with privacy as the stated point of difference.

What to watch

For diaspora households, the practical detail is the launch list: India is a day-one market, and Siri AI launches in English across the US, Australia, Canada, India, New Zealand, Singapore, South Africa and the UK. The open questions are commercial, not technical — whether the daily AI limits and the future fee for expanded access erode the value of a $299 screen, and whether a shared display that asks for a paired phone nearby delivers enough on its own. Reviews after the November 13 launch will answer the second question first.
